segments.content:
Chapter 186/0183 Inviting a Master Novelist to Make a Game

"Lightning! Pang Tong, link them all."

"No Plum Blossom."

"Dammit, don't share your hands. Attack!"

"Don't attack Pang Tong! What if he uses Nirvana and draws a few Plum Blossoms?"

Near the Triangle, a group of students was playing cards.

On a pop-up banner next to them were promotional slogans like "Board Game Club Recruiting New Members" and "Student Chen Guiliang Appointed Vice President."

The "Peking University Board Game Club," whose establishment was applied for last semester, was now finally starting to recruit.

The founder was named Tan Kaixuan, a second-year history student and a die-hard fan of *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*.

To attract more members, Tan Kaixuan had also invited Chen Guiliang. Besides making Chen Guiliang the vice president, he also had to come and sit at the recruitment booth every day at noon.

During the first two days of recruitment, the number of sign-ups for the Board Game Club was on par with the Mountain Eagle Club and the May Fourth Club. Even a large number of senior students came to sign up; they had long been discussing forming a club in the *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* interest group on the campus network.

"Excuse me, what kind of club is the Board Game Club? Why are so many people lining up to join?"

"The Tabletop Game Research Club. Ever heard of *Yu-Gi-Oh!* and *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*?"

"No."

"Both of those are tabletop games. *Legends of the Three Kingdoms* was invented by Chen Guiliang, a second-year senior. You must have heard of Chen Guiliang, right?"

"No."

"What the heck, where are you from? Senior Chen Guiliang is only a second-year, but he's already a multimillionaire."

"Huh? Is his dad a big boss?"

"He was a left-behind child, started from scratch!"

"Oh, then I'll sign up too."

"You've never even played a tabletop game, why are you joining the Board Game Club?"

"It just sounds really impressive. Is Senior Chen Guiliang here?"

"He's the one over there in the white T-shirt and blue jeans, playing cards with the new members."

At this moment, Senior Chen was a bit exasperated. "Can you guys please not reveal your roles?"

"I just casually said I'm a loyalist. Whoever wants to believe it can believe it," said a freshman who had just joined the club.

Another third-year student laughed, "CEO Chen, we're announcing our roles, what are you getting so worked up about? You're not the spy, are you?"

The freshman in seat four said, "He must be the spy. Let's focus our fire and kill him first. A true man should carry a three-foot sword and achieve immortal deeds! Heavenly Justice!"

"Damn, you said the wrong line. That's Taishi Ci's line when he's killed."

"I just like this line. What's wrong with that? Serves you right for being a busybody, I'll attack you too. Attack!"

"I'm speechless. I'm a rebel too, why are you attacking me?"

The scene of the in-person game was incredibly lively and the atmosphere was particularly cheerful.

This was especially true for the freshmen who had previously only played *Legends of the Three Kingdoms Online*. They had just entered university and already found so many fellow enthusiasts, and they could even play cards with the inventor, Chen Guiliang.

The feeling was simply too awesome to describe.

After playing a few consecutive rounds, Chen Guiliang said his goodbyes with a smile and left.

As he pedaled his beat-up bicycle past the recruitment booths of various clubs, someone would always shout at him, "CEO Chen, what about the sponsorship you promised last year?"

"Have your external relations department come talk to us. And don't go to the wrong place, it's Game Science, not ByteDance," Chen Guiliang responded.

What goes around comes around.

Last year, to promote *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, Chen Guiliang had gone around to other clubs handing out physical card decks and promised to sponsor those clubs this year.

He could have gone back on his word, but that would be too cheap.

Game Science's financial situation was currently good, but Peking University had too many clubs to sponsor all at once. He could only sponsor two or three each month, which wouldn't affect Game Science's funds and would also maintain a long-term presence at Peking University.

As Chen Guiliang passed the Triangle bulletin board, he noticed a large crowd of students gathered there.

He curiously pedaled his bike closer. Although he couldn't squeeze through, he could hear the students discussing "Li Ao."

"Li Ao is coming to Peking University?" Chen Guiliang asked a student who had just finished reading the poster.

The student said, "Next Wednesday, 9:30 AM, Li Ao will be giving a speech in the auditorium of the administration building."

Chen Guiliang's eyes lit up when he heard this. He could invite Li Ao to join Kaixin001!

This was Li Ao's first return to the mainland, and the whole event was called the "Li Ao Cultural Tour of China."

It was causing a huge sensation.

The first stop was the Forbidden City, where he would write the four characters "休戚与共" (sharing weal and woe). 休 (xiū) represented happiness, 戚 (qī) represented sorrow, and 共 (gòng) represented our Party.

The third stop was Peking University.

After that, he would also visit Tsinghua and Fudan.

The final stop was Hong Kong, where he was met with刁钻 tricky questions from the Hong Kong media. Li Ao publicly stated that "the mainland has never suppressed Hong Kong," and advised the people of Hong Kong to cooperate rather than confront.

Chen Guiliang rode his bike straight to Director Zhu's office. After waiting for half an hour, Director Zhu finally arrived for work.

"Don't tell me you're not confident about your make-up exams and want me to put in a good word with the professors?" Director Zhu said with a smile.

Chen Guiliang flatly denied it, "Absolutely not!"

"Then what are you here for?" Director Zhu asked. "You, the big boss, don't visit without a reason."

Chen Guiliang said, "Isn't Li Ao coming to Peking University for a speech? I'd like to get a seat near the front."

Director Zhu said, "That can be arranged. Remember, when you interact with Li Ao, be moderate in your speech. Otherwise, don't come looking for me next time!"

"I know my limits," Chen Guiliang said.

Compared to the radical students at Peking University, Chen Guiliang's way of speaking was practically gentle.

If Kaixin001 could get Li Ao, the effect would be absolutely powerful!

The celebrities were all too lazy. Chen Guiliang had also invited Liu Xuan, the Olympic champion and film star. Out of consideration for their senior-junior relationship at the same university, Liu Xuan had readily agreed to join Kaixin001, but in over a month, she had only posted once.

It was very likely that after Liu Xuan went off to film a movie, without a computer around for a long time, she had probably forgotten her account password...

He had to send someone to visit the film set, teach Liu Xuan how to post on Weibo with her phone, and while at it, help her "recall" her account and password.

Xie Yang was currently forming a relevant team.

He had them collect information on various film sets and then go to the sets to contact actors. They didn't have to be big stars; second, third, or fourth-tier actors would do as well.

This was especially true for young actors with some fame, as they could afford good phones and were more receptive to new things. Moreover, they often felt bored on set and could use their free time during filming to take selfies and post on Weibo to relieve their boredom.

Was the process complicated?

They would teach them step by step!

In the afternoon, Chen Guiliang arrived at the company.

The customer service department delivered a summary report: many users were reporting that they couldn't receive Weibo MMS photos.

Regarding this, Chen Guiliang could only feel helpless.

The compatibility was too poor; sending MMS between phones of different brands often failed.

This was a common problem in the industry.

After a long wait, the representative from Monternet, with whom Chen Guiliang had a prior appointment, finally showed up.

The moment they met, the Monternet representative said, "We overlooked the Weibo service, and we now need to re-establish the billing standards. For fans to receive Weibo text messages, they must subscribe to a 10 yuan monthly service. To receive Weibo MMS messages, they must subscribe to a 15 yuan monthly service. We will create a dedicated SP service number for Weibo. Users can subscribe to a plan by sending the relevant text message to the service number."

Well, well, users still had to pay to receive Weibo messages...

And Chen Guiliang had no choice but to accept, at most he could haggle a bit.

Monternet was a monopoly; businesses had no power to refuse!

After much back-and-forth, the monthly fee for text messages was reduced to 8 yuan, and the monthly fee for MMS was reduced to 12 yuan. Users could choose to subscribe to only one of the services.

After seeing the Monternet representative off, Chen Guiliang cursed, "Dammit, first they said receiving messages would be free, and now they're charging again. It was their own oversight, but it makes us look like we stole money from China Mobile."

Ao Yanchen guessed, "It's probably because a product like Weibo was just launched, and its user base wasn't large, and it was still user-to-user messaging. When Monternet reformed their fee structure, they probably missed us. Now that they've found the loophole, they rushed over to patch it. I estimate China Unicom will come knocking in a few days too."

"Forget it," Chen Guiliang said helplessly. "Anyway, we get a cut from those user subscriptions, so our profitability will increase. It's just not conducive to the rapid promotion of Weibo."

"CEO Chen."

His secretary, Hu Yuexia, walked over. "A call came from Game Science. They said your guest has arrived."

Chen Guiliang turned and left again, taking the elevator to the 10th floor, to Game Science's new office space.

A young man was sitting in the reception room.

His name was Hu Geng, and his pen name was Shuxia Yehu. He was a Peking University senior who had graduated several years ago.

For the game benchmarked against *DNF*, a complete story and world-building were needed, and Chen Guiliang couldn't possibly make everything up himself.

And as soon as Shuxia Yehu heard it was about making a game, he asked about the salary and immediately flew over.

He used to be a game planner!

*Chronicles of Finding Gods* was originally a game, and its factions and skill settings were all part of the game design. It was just that the game had been canceled before it was finished. He felt it would be a waste, so he rewrote it as a novel.

"Senior Hu, hello!"

"Hello."

The two shook hands in the reception room.

Shuxia Yehu was not a man of many words. After a few pleasantries, he asked, "You mentioned wanting to make an online game in the style of a side-scrolling arcade game. What's the specific gameplay?"

Chen Guiliang said, "The game is divided into safe zones and dungeons. In safe zones, you can accept quests, learn skills, buy equipment, and so on. It's the daily activity area for humans. Outside the safe zones, however, is occupied by various monsters. Players fight monsters by entering dungeons."

"Then where is the PvP arena located?" Shuxia Yehu asked.

"In the Colosseum," Chen Guiliang said. "You've played arcade fighting games, right?"

Shuxia Yehu said, "I think I understand."

Chen Guiliang explained:

"The general world view is that a catastrophe occurred on a planet, destroying human civilization, and countless monsters now fill the land. Humans can only start over, continuously excavating and restoring technology. They are already able to manufacture firearms."

"But in this process, people also discovered spiritual energy or magic, or even the power of faith. Some people purely cultivate spells or magic, some use that power to temper their bodies, and others cultivate through faith."

"For example, faith-based cultivators include priests, monks, Daoist masters, and so on. Their techniques are all different, but they can all counter dark-type monsters."

"Firearms and spells can also be combined, enchanting bullets..."

"There are those who fight with weapons like sabers, swords, and staves..."

"There are summoners, puppet masters, onmyoji..."

"There are pure martial artists who fight with their bodies; you can design all sorts of fist styles. Besides Chinese martial arts, there's also Western boxing, karate, judo, and so on."

"There are also mage-type characters, including Western mages and Eastern cultivators..."

"You will need to work with the data planners to design the classes and combat system. You also need to write a complete story plot, and design individual story characters, monsters, and dungeons..."

"If you have time, you can also serialize a novel on Qidian to build up hype for this game. The serialization royalties will be yours. As this is a work-for-hire, the copyright and authorship rights belong to the company. But the book royalties for the novel will also be yours; the company won't take a cent. If Qidian won't release the copyright, then we'll serialize it for free and not sign with them. Moreover, we'll serialize it for free on all major websites simultaneously. Once it gets popular, I'll help you find a publisher."

Shuxia Yehu carefully pondered the information Chen Guiliang had just given him. "I will do my best to write it well."

(End of this chapter)
